question: Should Gateway IPv6 support change existing `lan`/`custom` bind semantics, add an explicit IPv6/dual-stack mode, or remain documented as IPv4-only behind a proxy or sidecar?
rationale: The implementation choice changes who can reach a non-loopback Gateway and could alter existing LAN/container behavior, so code inspection cannot safely choose the exposure contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define explicit IPv6 or dual-stack contract
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved contract for IPv6 exposure, including auth/origin/firewall expectations and tests for LAN, custom, container, and platform-specific behavior.

options.title: Change existing LAN/custom semantics
options.body: Treat `lan` and/or `customBindHost` as IPv6-capable by default, accepting the upgrade and platform risk as intentional product direction.

options.title: Keep IPv4-only BYOH documented
options.body: Leave native Gateway BYOH binds IPv4-only and continue directing IPv6-only deployments to an IPv4 sidecar, reverse proxy, or host-network workaround.

recommendation.title: Define explicit IPv6 or dual-stack contract
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved contract for IPv6 exposure, including auth/origin/firewall expectations and tests for LAN, custom, container, and platform-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the clearest recent history across Gateway bind/listen behavior and adjacent security hardening.
